task.title: Handle an angry guest whose room is not ready
task.brief: Imagine you are at the front desk of a hotel in Bengaluru. Mr. Joseph Mathew has a confirmed booking. He arrives at 2 pm (check-in time) after a long flight. His room is not ready because housekeeping is late. He is tired and angry, and says he has a work call in 45 minutes. Speak for 60 to 90 seconds as if you are talking to him. A good answer: greet him and use his name, listen and apologise sincerely, explain simply what happened without blaming staff, give clear options (for example a quiet place for his call, Wi-Fi, a drink, luggage help, a time when the room will be ready, or another room), and close politely by telling him what you will do next.
key_points: Greets the guest politely and uses his name
Shows understanding of his tiredness and urgent call
Offers practical options: quiet place for the call, Wi-Fi, refreshment, luggage storage
Gives a clear time the room will be ready or offers another room
Promises a follow-up and closes politely

rubric.label: Greeting and structure
rubric.guide: 0 = no greeting, jumbled, 3 = greets but loose order, 5 = greets by name, apologises, gives options, closes clearly

rubric.label: Right actions
rubric.guide: 0 = wrong or no solution, 3 = one weak option, 5 = practical options for his call and a clear room time

rubric.label: Empathy
rubric.guide: 0 = cold or argues, 3 = polite but flat, 5 = calm, warm and shows he is understood

rubric.label: Clarity
rubric.guide: 0 = hard to follow, 3 = mostly clear, 5 = short, clear sentences a tired guest can follow
